title: On-call & Incident Response: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Comms Templates
author: Sofia Ramirez
summary: Company-standard incident lifecycle, severity taxonomy, escalation matrix, runbook templates, postmortem requirements, on-call rotations, game day guidance, and customer communication templates for Redwood Inference.
content:
Purpose and scope

This document defines Redwood Inference's standardized approach to on-call and incident response. It covers: incident severity & taxonomy, alerting and escalation policies, runbook structure and examples, postmortem expectations, on-call rotations and responsibilities, game day exercise guidance, status page and customer communication templates, and operational metrics to track. This is the canonical reference for engineering teams and SREs.

Audience

- Primary: on-call engineers, SREs, service owners.
- Secondary: product managers, customer success, support, and legal for customer-facing comms.

Definitions and goals

- Incident: any event causing user-visible degradation, data loss, or security exposure.
- Goal: restore customer functionality safely and quickly, communicate clearly, and learn to prevent recurrence.
- Key measurable objectives: Mean Time To Detect (MTTD), Mean Time To Restore (MTTR), percentage of incidents with actionable postmortems, and change re-introduction rate.

Severity levels (taxonomy)

- Sev 0 (SEV0 - Critical): Complete outage of core hosted API or Dedicated cluster impacting >50% of production requests or an incident causing material revenue loss or regulatory exposure. Target RRT (Respond & Restore Time): 15 minutes response.
- Sev 1 (High): Significant degradation (e.g., sustained latency 5x SLO for >5 minutes for a major route, or an outage impacting a single customer with no mitigation). Target response: 30 minutes.
- Sev 2 (Medium): Partial degradation or feature loss with acceptable workarounds (e.g., degraded observability, spooler lag). Target response: 4 hours.
- Sev 3 (Low): Minor issue, no customer impact, or non-urgent maintenance items. Response by next-business-day.

Alerting and detection

- Monitoring sources: Prometheus metrics, tracing alerts (Jaeger), log-based alerts (Splunk/Elasticsearch), RUM/customer error reports, and PagerDuty triggers.
- Alert routing: Alerts map to services via our Alert Manager config. Critical alerts must page the on-call rotation and an escalation target (team lead).
- Alert runbook link: All alerts include a direct link to the primary runbook and a short play to triage (one-click from alert).

Escalation matrix

1. Primary on-call engineer pages and responds within severity target (see taxonomy).
2. If primary cannot respond in severity window, PagerDuty auto-escalates to secondary (10 minutes for SEV0, 20 minutes for SEV1).
3. Escalate to service owner / team lead after two failed responses or if the incident spans multiple teams.
4. For SEV0, notify Head of Platform and Customer Success within 30 minutes.

Roles & responsibilities

- Primary on-call: Triage, initial mitigation, runbook actions, incident state updates.
- Secondary on-call: Backup for paging / deep-dive support.
- Service owner: Coordinates cross-team work and deployment decisions.
- Incident commander (IC): Assigned for SEV0/SEV1 to coordinate response, communications, warroom.
- Communications lead: Writes and posts internal and external updates.

Runbook standards and template

All services must have a runbook with the following flat fields (documented in Confluence and referenced in alerts):
- Summary: 1–2 sentence description of the service and impact symptoms.
- Detection: list of alerts/metrics that indicate this incident class.
- PagerDuty alert + severity mapping: exact PD escalation policy name.
- Quick triage checklist: steps 1–5 to determine scope and cause.
- Mitigations: safe actions that reduce customer impact (with commands).
- Recovery steps: full resolution steps, including rollback commands, configuration keys, and post-restart validations.
- Postmortem link: placeholder to link after the incident.
- Owner and secondary contacts: on-call rotation + service owner.

Runbook example (excerpt)

Summary:
Redwood API gateway request timeout spike. Symptoms: 5xx rate > 2% for > 2 minutes and 99p latency > 1.5x SLO.

Quick triage checklist:
1. Confirm alert and timeframe: 
   - kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=api-gateway
   - curl -s https://prometheus/api/v1/query_range?query=rate(http_requests_total[5m])
2. Check deployment & rolling restarts: kubectl rollout status deployment/api-gateway -n prod
3. Look for increase in 502/504 in ELB access logs (S3 path).
4. If error spikes coincide with a recent deployment (<30m), roll back: kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-gateway -n prod
5. If CPU/GPU pressure: scale up replicas and trigger autoscaling policy: kubectl scale deployment/api-gateway --replicas=6 -n prod

Mitigations (safe):
- Toggle feature flag (ff-api-slow-path) via config service: curl -X POST ${CONFIG_SERVICE}/flags/ff-api-slow-path -d '{"state":"off"}'
- Apply temporary traffic-shed rule on router: rtrctl block-route --service api-gateway --percentage 20

Recovery checks:
- 99p latency < 1.2x SLO for 10 minutes
- 5xx rate < 0.5%
- Logs show successful healthcheck responses from all gateway instances

Postmortem process & template

When to write a postmortem:
- All SEV0 and SEV1 incidents require a blameless, public postmortem within 7 business days. SEV2 incidents require a short incident summary; SEV3 optional.

Postmortem required fields (flat list in Confluence page):
- Incident title, severity, start/end times (UTC), duration.
- Summary of impact (customers affected, functionality impacted).
- Timeline of key events (timestamped).
- Root cause analysis (RCA): factual findings only.
- Corrective actions (short-term mitigations) and preventive actions (long-term). Owner and ETA for each action.
- Rollback or change history if relevant.
- What went well and what to improve.
- Link to runbook, runbook gaps, and ticket references.

Postmortem example excerpt:
- Title: SEV0 — Hosted API 99p latency spike — 2026-02-05
- Timeline highlights: 2026-02-05T09:41Z (alert), 09:45Z (IC assigned), 09:52Z (temporary feature flag rollback), 10:12Z (service healthy).
- Root cause: regression introduced by gateway connection pool change in release v2.14.0.
- Preventive action: add pre-deploy perf test for gateway with 95th/99th pt checks; owner: QA Infra (Morgan Liu), ETA: 2026-03-15.

Ownership and tracking

- All postmortem actions are tracked in Jira with label incident-RCA and assigned owners. Each action must have an ETA within 30 days or be escalated to the IC.
- SRE lead reviews all SEV0/SEV1 postmortems and closes the incident in the incident tracker when actions are assigned.

On-call rotations & guidelines

- Rotation cadence: two-week rotations for primary on-call for SRE and service teams. Secondary on-call is a one-week rotation for deep-dive availability.
- Handoff checklist (end of shift): 
  1. Check active incidents and open follow-ups.
  2. Confirm runbook links are correct and add notes to the on-call log.
  3. Notify successor via Slack #oncall and call if handing off during an active incident.
- Vacation & swap policy: Owners must update PagerDuty before starting leave; swaps require PD and team lead approval.

Game day exercises and readiness

- Frequency: each critical service must run at least one game day per quarter.
- Goals: validate runbooks, verify escalation chain, and test cross-team coordination.
- Typical game day steps:
  1. Scope & objectives defined by service owner.
  2. Inject failure (traffic spike, partial instance kill, network partition) in staging or isolated canary.
  3. Run primary on-call through live runbook steps; time-to-detect and time-to-mitigate are recorded.
  4. Document gaps, update runbooks, and create follow-up tickets.

Status page and customer communications templates

Principles:
- Timely: initial external notice within 30 minutes for SEV0 affecting customers.
- Honest and actionable: include what is impacted, mitigation steps, and ETA.
- Avoid speculation: updates should state facts and next steps.

Status page template (external):
- Title: [Incident] Partial outage of Redwood Hosted API — {start_time}
- Impact: Customers may experience increased latency or 5xx errors for text-generation endpoints in region {region}.
- Status: Identified / Investigating / Mitigating / Recovering / Resolved
- Latest update: {timestamp} — {short factual update}
- Next update: {ETA or "as available"}
- Contact: support@redwood.ai (for affected customers)

Internal customer email template (to Customer Success/Sales to forward):
- Subject: Incident update: {short title} — {status} — {timestamp}
- Body: Hello {CustomerName},
  We are investigating an issue impacting {product area}. We have identified {impact summary}. Our engineers are working on mitigation and we will provide the next update by {ETA}. For urgent concerns contact {CS rep contact}.
  Thank you for your patience,
  Redwood Inference Support

Developer-facing incident update (Slack + internal status page):
- Short post format: [SEV{n}] {service} — {current-status} — {1 line impact} — {link to warroom / incident page}
- Warroom items: incident timeline, runbook link, command snippets, deploy links, PD incident ID.

Communication ownership and cadence

- IC or communications lead posts internal updates every 15 minutes for SEV0, every 30 minutes for SEV1, and hourly thereafter until resolved.
- External updates: initial within 30 minutes for SEV0, then every hour until recovery. For SEV1, initial within 2 hours.

SLOs, metrics and dashboards to maintain

- Per-service SLOs (examples): 99p latency < 600ms for /v1/generate (hosted api), availability 99.95% monthly.
- Dashboards: per-route latency percentiles, error-rate heatmaps, request volume & throttling, queue/backlog depth, and infrastructure health.
- Post-incident metrics: MTTD, MTTR, number of customers impacted, number of follow-ups created, and time to close follow-ups.

Templates & CLI snippets (copyable)

- Open incident page: curl -X POST https://confluence.api.internal/pages -d '{"title":"Incident: {title}","space":"oncall-and-incident-response" }'
- Trigger PG escalation (example PD API): curl -X POST https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents -H 'Authorization: Token token={PD_TOKEN}' -d '{"service":"svc_123","title":"SEV0 - {summary}"}'

Post-incident review & continuous improvement

- All teams must allocate up to 8 hours per month for post-incident follow-ups and runbook maintenance.
- The SRE leadership holds a monthly incident review meeting to review SEV0/SEV1 trends and status of corrective actions.

Appendix: quick checklist for new on-call engineers

1. Ensure PagerDuty and Slack notifications are enabled and test paging.
2. Know where your team's runbooks live and verify links.
3. Read the SLOs for your services.
4. Familiarize yourself with rollback and mitigation commands.
5. Run a local conformance test with the staging warbook once before first shift.
